newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African opposition criticises truth commission.
newsitem.headline: S.African opposition criticises truth commission.

text.p: South Africa's two main opposition parties accused Archbishop Desmond Tutu's truth commission on Monday of bias in its quest to uncover apartheid human rights abuses.

The separate accusations from the National Party (NP) of F.W. de Klerk and the Inkatha Freedom Party of Mangosuthu Buthelezi followed a row last week in which the NP said the commission was favouring the African National Congress.
The NP began an indefinite boycott of the commission and said it might take the body to court on the grounds it was violating legislative requirements that it act impartially and objectively.
Inkatha, main black rivals of President Nelson Mandela's ANC, said on Monday it was not surprised by the NP's boycott.
"The Truth and Reconciliation Commission has strayed from its mandate and become increasingly partisan in its operations," an Inkatha statement said.
"The workings of the commission have turned into media-type trials which are a travesty of justice...The ANC sympathies of the commission are patent," it said.
The NP introduced a motion in parliament on Monday urging Tutu and his fellow-commissioners "to act at all times impartially, without showing any political or other bias".

Tutu last week criticised De Klerk's latest evidence to the commission, saying it was hard to believe the former white president's assertion that human rights abuses during apartheid had been aberrations that violated government policy.
Tutu later sought to counter NP accusations of bias by saying he had played a behind-the-scenes role in helping De Klerk win the Nobel peace prize in 1993. He was named joint winner with Mandela.
